claim: retina (Rust RTSP client, MIT/Apache-2.0, 0.4.21 released 2026-10-04, repository active) writes camera H.264 streams to MP4 and is in production use in Moonfire NVR.
Continuous FFmpeg segment recording with retention is a production pattern: Frigate (MIT, active) records camera streams to segments and applies retention modes.

GStreamer's va plugin offers hardware H.264 encode (vah264enc, vah264lpenc), post-processing for scale/crop (vapostproc) and a hardware compositor (vacompositor); GStreamer is LGPL and gstreamer-rs 0.25.4 is MIT OR Apache-2.0.
The Intel Media Driver (MIT/BSD-3-Clause) supports AVC hardware encode on Alder Lake-N, with HuC low-power encode from Linux 6.2; an LGPL FFmpeg build must not enable GPL parts such as libx264.
The Jetson Orin NX 16GB box (reComputer J4012) encodes up to 12 × 1080p30 H.265 in hardware.

The Intel N150 has a 24-EU integrated GPU at 1 GHz on a single memory channel; the ONNX Runtime OpenVINO execution provider can run models on that iGPU in FP16. Throughput for a 4-court shot judge is unmeasured.
The Jetson Orin NX 16GB is rated at 157 TOPS.

Every O-2 component on the box and online side exists as a maintained Rust crate with a permissive licence (axum, tokio, retina, gstreamer, ort, rusqlite, askama, argon2, sqlx, aws-sdk-s3, aws-sdk-sesv2, totp-rs), so both sides are written in one language.
Frigate's code base is roughly 5.2 MB of Python plus 4.9 MB of TypeScript.

At the BSP reference rate of PHP 63.10 per USD, hardware per court on a 12-court venue is ₱9,733 with an Intel N150 box (US$385 per 4 courts) and a US$57.99 PoE camera, versus ₱25,729 with a Jetson Orin NX box (US$1,399 per 4 courts).
Ubuntu 26.04 LTS is supported to 2031-05-29, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS to 2029-05-31, Debian 12 to 2028-06-30, PostgreSQL 18 to 2030-11-14 and Python 3.14 to 2030-10-31.
JetPack 7, the current Jetson software stack for Orin, is built on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS; keeping a box patched past May 2029 needs Ubuntu Pro at US$500 per server machine per year.
The newest ort release is a release candidate (2.0.0-rc.15, 2026-10-19) and axum is still a 0.x series (0.8.9), so API changes are likely within a 3-year horizon.

Under the year-1 upper-bound usage model the online part costs about US$68 a month: R2 storage ≈ US$24.60 with free egress, R2 requests ≈ US$2.50, SES ≈ US$14.40, a 2 GiB droplet US$12 and managed PostgreSQL US$15.15.
RAUC provides redundant A/B slot updates with boot confirmation and bootloader fallback, and systemd-sysupdate provides A/B versioned file or partition transfers.
Every pinned crate and PyPI package carries an MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause or MIT OR Apache-2.0 licence and has no advisories.
retina describes itself as having "many missing features"; its tracker has open camera-specific failures (V380 DESCRIBE EOF, Eufy lost RTP packets) and a planned 0.5 breaking release.
OSV reports zero vulnerabilities for every pinned crate and PyPI package version, and deps.dev lists no advisory keys for them.
Forge built and released Jss-on/watchman, an offline Rust 2024 camera monitor using ort 2.0.0-rc.12, rusqlite and argon2; its NVIDIA GPU path is tested on Windows only.
LLM-generated code quality differs by up to 84 % across libraries with similar functions, so harness proficiency must be measured on the chosen stack.
ort exposes CUDA, TensorRT, OpenVINO and QNN execution providers, and the OpenVINO provider targets Intel CPU, GPU and NPU, so ONNX models can move between boards.
Frigate's container ships GPL FFmpeg builds and is based on debian:12.
Ultralytics YOLO is AGPL-3.0 unless an Enterprise licence is bought, so it cannot be used under the keep-the-code-private rule.
Forge has delivered Python web back ends (Django) for school-insight-v2 and npo-accounting-v2.
